purpose: Project-specific model selection before any production model or pool allocation change.
context_policy: Each candidate receives the same task prompt and the same task-scoped repository context files; no model receives benchmark-only hints.

tasks.title: Add a bounded unit test for calculator behavior
tasks.prompt: Add one focused regression test for the calculator behavior represented by the existing implementation. Return only structured JSON containing summary, touched_paths, and a unified diff. Do not modify production code.

tasks.title: Tighten a bounded parsing edge case
tasks.prompt: Propose the smallest safe fix for one malformed labeled connection-ID parsing edge case. Preserve additive import semantics and existing lifecycle rules. Return structured JSON with rationale, touched_paths, and unified diff.

tasks.title: Explain a single-file documentation change
tasks.prompt: As a leader, decide the minimum safe action for a documentation-only clarification. Return structured JSON with classification, objective, one-step plan, validation, and stop conditions.

tasks.title: Produce a bounded validation decision
tasks.prompt: Given a successful execution checkpoint and passed independent validation evidence, return the minimum structured decision needed to admit a WorkerWorkProduct to the next Core boundary. Do not authorize mutation by yourself.

tasks.title: Multi-file lifecycle validation repair
tasks.prompt: Design the smallest multi-file repair for a credential lifecycle validation boundary where metadata and protected credential state can disagree. Preserve stable connection identity, never read TXT after import, and never expose raw credentials. Return structured JSON with rationale, touched_paths, and unified diff.

tasks.title: Cross-module readiness read model
tasks.prompt: Improve the connection readiness read model so a stored-but-unassigned connection is never shown as routing-ready while an assigned, validated, credential-present connection is clearly ready. Preserve config/registry.json as authority and do not add auto-assignment. Return structured JSON and unified diff.

tasks.title: Debug a multi-module provider failure
tasks.prompt: Analyze a provider failure observed after several runtime retries. Identify evidence gaps, likely root causes, bounded investigation order, and conditions for SAFE_STOP versus recovery. Return a structured leadership decision.

tasks.title: Routing failover repair
tasks.prompt: Design a production-safe routing repair for complete primary-pool exhaustion that must fail over to the configured failover pool and SAFE_STOP after complete exhaustion. Preserve authoritative registry ownership and existing leases. Return structured JSON and unified diff.

tasks.title: WorkerWorkProduct integrity repair
tasks.prompt: Repair a hypothetical WorkerWorkProduct integrity gap. The result must bind task_id, worker_id, changed_targets, validation checkpoint, and execution checkpoint; raw stdout/stderr must remain outside the authoritative work product. Return structured JSON and unified diff.

tasks.title: Architecture-level recovery planning
tasks.prompt: Develop a recovery strategy for a project where all current leader credentials are failed and one complex worker pool is degraded. Preserve stable IDs, explicit registry authority, independent validation, authorization boundaries, and SAFE_STOP semantics. Return structured JSON with assumptions, dependency order, recovery paths, stop conditions, and verification evidence.

tasks.title: Security-sensitive lifecycle orchestration
tasks.prompt: Propose a safe multi-step implementation plan for a security-sensitive credential rotation and validation flow. Preserve redaction, protected storage, stable identity, routing authority, and fail-closed behavior. Return structured JSON and a bounded patch only if an implementation change is required.

tasks.title: Project understanding and gap analysis
tasks.prompt: Act as the Central Leader for this repository. Build a project understanding, identify the highest-impact remaining gaps, and propose a minimal evidence-driven plan. Do not claim completion without evidence. Return structured JSON.

tasks.title: Requirement interpretation and decomposition
tasks.prompt: Interpret the supplied requirements and decompose them into bounded tasks with dependencies, validation criteria, risk classification, and explicit stop conditions. Do not invent requirements or bypass Core authority. Return structured JSON.

tasks.title: Authorization-aware planning
tasks.prompt: Given a request that may require mutation, produce an authorization-aware plan that separates user intent, leader plan, worker work-product, independent validation, execution authorization, and verified result. Explicitly state when SAFE_STOP is mandatory. Return structured JSON.

tasks.title: Dependency and risk analysis
tasks.prompt: Analyze the dependency and failure graph for a multi-module autonomous engineering task. Identify critical path, recovery options, evidence requirements, and conflicts. Prefer the smallest safe execution sequence. Return structured JSON.

tasks.title: Recovery strategy under partial failure
tasks.prompt: Plan recovery when multiple provider connections and one worker role are degraded. Preserve fail-closed safety, stable connection identity, configured pools, independent validation, and authorization boundaries. Return structured JSON.

evaluation_contract.structured_output: Every response must parse into the benchmark envelope; leader tasks have required decision fields, code tasks have bounded touched_paths plus unified diff.
evaluation_contract.tool_use: Tool-call cases use a fixed mock-tool schema; correctness is determined by tool name, argument validity, order, and unnecessary calls.
evaluation_contract.code_execution: Code patches are applied only to a disposable temporary copy, never the working tree or production registry.
evaluation_contract.regression: Only task-declared focused tests are executed after a patch is applied to the temporary copy.
evaluation_contract.security: No credential files are read by the benchmark corpus; the runner must obtain provider credentials only through the existing protected secret-store abstraction and must never print them.
